NEW DELHI: Former Tehelka editor-in-chief Tarun Tejpal surrendered before the Mapusa court on Monday after the Bombay high court sentenced him to 10 years in prison for raping a junior colleague in a hotel lift in Goa in 2013.Tejpal had challenged the high court’s verdict in the Supreme Court , which directed him to surrender within two weeks. The high court’s ruling on August 6 overturned his acquittal by a Goa sessions court in 2021 and convicted him of the offence.The Supreme Court’s direction means Tejpal must begin serving his sentence, subject to any further orders in his appeal.The case relates to allegations that Tejpal sexually assaulted a junior colleague inside a hotel elevator in November 2013 during an event organised by Tehelka magazine.A Goa sessions court acquitted him of all charges in May 2021, saying the prosecution had failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. The Goa government challenged that decision before the Bombay High Court, which later overturned the acquittal and imposed a 10-year rigorous imprisonment sentence.Tejpal approached the Supreme Court through advocate Aditya Samaddar. The Goa government has also challenged the high court’s sentence, seeking life imprisonment on the grounds that the punishment was inadequate considering the seriousness of the offences.
Article Summary: Former Tehelka editor-in-chief Tarun Tejpal surrendered before the Mapusa court on Monday. NEW DELHI: Israel on Monday wished India a happy Hindi Diwas , calling Hindi an "ancient language" that is "still very much alive today"."Two ancient languages, still very much alive today. Israel would like to wish everyone हिंदी दिवस की हार्दिक शुभकमनाएं!," Reuven Azar, Israel's ambassador to India, wrote on X.Union home minister Amit Shah on Monday extended heartfelt greetings to citizens on the occasion of Hindi Diwas, highlighting the role of the language in public communication, good governance and national integration, while calling for the empowerment of all Indian languages.In a post on X, HM Shah said, “Heartfelt greetings to all fellow citizens on Hindi Diwas. As the official language, Hindi is playing a vital role in strengthening public communication, good governance, and national integration.”“Hindi, which moves forward alongside all Indian languages, is now also becoming the language of technology and research. On the occasion of Official Language Day, I pay my respects to all the great personalities who have made an unforgettable contribution to enriching Hindi. Let us, on this occasion, resolve to empower all Indian languages, including Hindi,” he added.Defence minister Rajnath Singh also extended his greetings, describing Hindi as an important expression of India’s culture, civilisation and values.Singh posted on X, “Hindi is not merely a language, but a powerful expression of India’s culture, civilization, and life values. It is the language that weaves our diversity into the thread of unity. Enhancing the glory of Hindi is an act of honoring our rich linguistic and cultural heritage. Let us resolve to preserve, promote, and propagate Hindi, and make it even more robust in the fields of knowledge, science, technology, and innovation.Heartfelt greetings to all Hindi enthusiasts on Hindi Diwas.”Hindi Diwas is observed every year on September 14 to commemorate the adoption of Hindi in the Devanagari script as the official language of the Union by the Constituent Assembly on September 14, 1949. The observance of Hindi Diwas began on September 14, 1953, and has continued since then.

NEW DELHI: Taking a stern view of a murder accused taking out a "victory procession" on being granted bail by Punjab and Haryana HC, Supreme Court has directed Haryana Police to produce him before it.A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta also recorded in its order that despite a non-bailable warrant being issued against the accused, he had not been produced in custody.The matter was taken up for hearing on Sept 8.Taking note of the counsel's submission that the accused, Vishal, had held a procession after getting bail and threatened witnesses, the bench directed the accused to surrender. During a heated exchange, Vishal allegedly hit several people with lathi and axe, grievously injuring several persons belonging to the complainant's side, one of whom died.Following this Vishal was arrested and kept in custody for over three years.The HC rejected Vishal's bail petition four times but accepted it the fifth time after it was pointed that material witnesses have been examined in the case and he has spent over three years in custody. Article Title: Amit Shah says decolonising knowledge not about erasing history, but reclaiming India's narrative
Article Text:
Amit Shah says decolonising India’s history means presenting it from an Indian perspective

‘True knowledge is never held hostage by an ideology’

Shah highlights manuscripts, proposes wider knowledge network

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday said decolonisation of India's history and knowledge does not mean erasing the past, but presenting historical truth authentically and from an Indian perspective.Shah made the remarks while inaugurating the 'Ganesh Gyanarthi' exhibition at the Asiatic Society of Mumbai. He said India's knowledge traditions, manuscripts and archives should be preserved and taken to people across the country and the world.“Decolonisation does not mean erasing history. From our perspective, it means presenting historical truth to the world in an authentic manner and from an Indian perspective,” Shah said, as cited by news agency PTI.He said the British had intertwined knowledge and power and argued that the task now was to free knowledge from that framework.“Today, we are moving forward to liberate knowledge from that and towards decolonisation,” Shah said.Shah said knowledge should remain free from ideological constraints and criticised the colonial interpretation of India's intellectual traditions.“True knowledge is never held hostage by an ideology. Knowledge itself is an ideology.If you bind it in any way, you change the very meaning of knowledge. Knowledge should be free and uninhibited, and its declaration should also be free and uninhibited,” he said, according to ANI.“India's knowledge was not being written in India's voice. India's knowledge was being written in the language of a colonial perspective,” Shah said.He said the focus should now be on using the wealth and collections preserved at the Asiatic Society for the creation of a “Great India”.“Rather than going into why the Asiatic Society was formed, who formed it, and for what purpose, we should move forward in the direction of how the wealth, knowledge, and collections gathered here can be used in the creation of a Great India (Mahaan Bharat),” he said.Shah highlighted the rare manuscripts preserved at the Asiatic Society, including an illustrated copy of the Mahabharata and texts related to Jainism and Buddhism.“A great deal of things are lying here, including an illustrated copy of the Mahabharata. Such texts of Jain Kalpasutra and Buddhism are hardly available anywhere else; such texts are lying here. Much knowledge is present here that should have come out a long time ago,” he said.Shah called on the new committee to expand the institution's reach by bringing scholars from Maharashtra and across India to study its collections. He also proposed bringing libraries and institutions preserving heritage across the country onto a common platform under the Asiatic Society.He suggested creating a shared pool of knowledge that could be made available to students, researchers and scholars.Shah further proposed a campaign to collect ancestral documents preserved in villages and households across Maharashtra and link them with the Gyan Bharatam manuscript survey.“Because within these manuscripts lies immense knowledge, and there is a need to conduct research on this knowledge. A great power to take the nation forward lies within them,” he said.Referring to Nalanda, Shah said attempts to destroy physical repositories could not eliminate knowledge preserved through memory and tradition.“One can burn the library of Nalanda... but the knowledge that resides in people's minds as memory and tradition (Smriti and Shruti)—no one can destroy that knowledge,” he said.Shah said the Asiatic Society should work with the government and institutions across India to preserve and share India's knowledge traditions. He urged the new team to use Indology for the welfare of the country and the wider world.
Article Summary: Union home minister Amit Shah said decolonisation of India's history and knowledge does not mean erasing the past. Shah made the remarks while inaugurating the 'Ganesh Gyanarthi' exhibition at the Asiatic Society of Mumbai. He said knowledge should remain free from ideological constraints.

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “Having a dad with a big name doesn’t do the work for you” - How Trinity Rodman rose above Dennis Rodman’s shadow, lived in motels, and built her own soccer legacy
Article Text:
Inspiring story of the day: “Having a dad with a big name doesn’t do the work for you” - How Trinity Rodman rose above Dennis Rodman’s shadow, lived in motels, and built her own soccer legacy

How did Trinity Rodman live in a car despite being Dennis Rodman’s daughter

Call Her Daddy

What did Trinity Rodman say about her relationship with Dennis Rodman

Why does Trinity Rodman call Michelle Moyer her role model?

How did Trinity Rodman turn a difficult childhood into a soccer career

Why is Trinity Rodman’s story inspiring beyond soccer

Trinity Rodman has built a soccer career that now stands on its own. The Washington Spirit star is a 2024 Olympic gold medalist, a 2021 NWSL champion and, as of January 2026, the highest-paid player in NWSL history. But her childhood looked very different from what many people expected from the daughter of NBA legend Dennis Rodman . Trinity and her brother DJ once lived with their mother, Michelle Moyer, in a Ford Expedition and cheap motels in Newport Beach. Through those difficult years, Michelle kept life feeling normal for her children. That bond helped shape Trinity into the player she is today.Having a famous father did not mean Trinity Rodman grew up with an easy life. After Dennis Rodman and Michelle Moyer separated, Trinity, her brother DJ and their mother faced serious money problems. For a period, they moved between a Ford Expedition and motels when Michelle could afford a room.The situation was especially strange because they were living in Newport Beach, where Trinity went to a wealthy school. She has spoken about seeing classmates arrive in expensive cars while her own family was trying to work out where they would stay.On, Trinity explained just how unusual those years were:“We had a Ford Expedition and we lived in that for a little bit. Mind you, in Newport Beach… So imagine living in a car going to a rich school when everybody else is in Rolls-Royces and Range Rovers. But my mom tried to make every situation seem smoother than it actually was. For me and DJ, it was never embarrassing because we had each other and we had our mom.”For Trinity and DJ, however, those memories were not only painful. Their mother tried hard to make sure they still had happy childhood moments. At motels, they could eat breakfast, use the pool and spend time together before school. That helped the children see their family life differently from how an outsider might have seen it.Trinity’s relationship with Dennis Rodman has remained one of the most talked-about parts of her story, but it has also been one of the most painful. She has said that her father was often absent while she was growing up and that there were long periods when they had little contact.That distance became impossible to ignore as Trinity began making a name for herself in soccer. Instead of being known only as an athlete, she was repeatedly asked about being Dennis Rodman’s daughter.She later spoke openly about how difficult that connection could feel:“He’s a person. He’s not a dad. Maybe by blood, but nothing else… Hearing his voice is painful because it’s missing him mixed with the fact that he’s an alcoholic. I answer the phone now for my conscience, but it took me a long time to realize that having a dad with a big name doesn’t do the work for you. I had to build everything myself.”Dennis has also publicly admitted that he was not the father he wanted to be. At his Basketball Hall of Fame induction, he said he wished he had been a better father.For Trinity, though, her own career could not depend on her father’s reputation. Her speed, finishing, attacking ability and work on the field became the things that made people remember her.If Dennis Rodman gave Trinity a famous last name, Michelle Moyer gave her the support that helped her grow into a professional athlete. Michelle raised Trinity and DJ largely as a single mother and remained closely involved in Trinity’s soccer journey.The Guardian reported in 2021 that Trinity saw her mother as her main support system. That feeling has remained central to how she talks about her childhood and her success.Trinity put it simply:“My mom wasn’t in the NBA, but she’s my role model. She is my world, my rock, and my right hand. She’s the strongest person I know. People always say, ‘Oh, you get your athleticism from your dad,’ but my work ethic, my heart, my grit, and the woman I am today-that’s 100% my mom.”That is an important part of Trinity Rodman’s story because her biggest influence was not another famous athlete. It was the person who was there when money was tight, when the family had nowhere stable to stay and when Trinity was still only a young girl trying to understand her world.Trinity’s soccer career moved quickly once she reached the professional level. She entered the NWSL with the Washington Spirit in 2021 and became the youngest player ever selected in the league’s draft at the time. She went on to win the NWSL Rookie of the Year award and helped the Spirit win the league championship that same year.Her rise continued with the U.S. women’s national team. She became an important attacking player for the USWNT and was part of the squad that won Olympic gold at the 2024 Paris Games.The success also changed the way her name was viewed. Instead of being introduced mainly as Dennis Rodman’s daughter, Trinity became a major soccer star in her own right.In January 2026, she reached another major point in her career when she re-signed with the Washington Spirit on a deal worth more than $2 million per year. The agreement made her the highest-paid player in NWSL history.That achievement says a lot about how far she has come. The girl who once went to school after sleeping in a car is now one of the biggest names in American women’s soccer.Trinity Rodman’s story is not simply about becoming famous despite having a difficult childhood. It is about how she chose to define herself.She could have spent her career being introduced through her father’s name. Instead, she has built an identity around her own performances and the people who stood beside her. Her mother remained a constant presence, while soccer gave Trinity a place where her effort could speak for itself.Her journey also explains why the success means more than trophies and contracts. The Olympic gold medal, NWSL championship and record-breaking deal are major achievements, but they came after years of work that had little to do with her father’s fame.Trinity has been clear about that point herself: a famous parent can give someone a name, but it cannot do the training, handle the pressure or play the game for them.For Trinity Rodman, the most important part of her legacy may be that she did not allow her father’s story to become her own. She took the difficult parts of her childhood, held on to the support her mother gave her and built a career that now belongs completely to her.
Article Summary: Trinity Rodman has built a soccer career that now stands on its own. The Washington Spirit star is a 2024 Olympic gold medalist, a 2021 NWSL champion and, as of January 2026, the highest-paid player in NWSL history. But her childhood looked very different from what many people expected from the daughter of NBA legend Dennis Rodman.

Article Title: Inspiring story on balancing motherhood and career:“You can achieve anything. You can be a part of anything that you want to”-How Brittany Mahomes continues to inspire her children

For Brittany Mahomes , motherhood did not mean putting her own ambitions on hold. Instead, becoming a mother of three appears to have changed the way she approaches both family and work. The wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes says her children have given her a stronger sense of purpose, while also pushing her to show them what it means to dream big and work hard.Brittany Mahomes entered motherhood while already building a life of her own. She had a background in soccer, fitness and business, while her relationship with Patrick Mahomes placed her close to the intense world of professional football.Then came a new role that changed everything.Brittany and Patrick welcomed their first child, daughter Sterling, in 2021. Their family grew again with the arrival of son Bronze in 2022 and daughter Golden in 2025.Three children later, Brittany says motherhood has changed more than her daily routine. It has influenced the way she thinks about her goals, her time and the example she wants to set at home.“Being a mom changed so many things in my life and changed how I looked at so many things,” Brittany, 30, told Yahoo Entertainment in June 2026. “It really reshaped and redefined a lot of things in my life.”That change does not sound like a retreat from ambition. If anything, Brittany appears to have found another reason to keep moving.She explained that motherhood has made her more deliberate about the opportunities she takes and the people and causes she gives her attention to. Her priorities have become clearer, with family now playing a major role in how she measures what is worth pursuing.That shift is especially meaningful for someone whose life has long been lived in the public eye.One of the strongest themes in Brittany Mahomes' recent comments is the importance of showing her children that their dreams should not come with unnecessary limits.“It’s made me more intentional, more purposeful and, honestly, more motivated to keep going and keep showing my kids that there are no boundaries in front of you. You can achieve anything. You can be a part of anything that you want to. You need to dream big and understand that you have to work hard and do the hard things to do the fun things.”There is a simple lesson behind those words. Brittany does not want her children to learn about ambition only through their father’s NFL career. She wants them to see it through her actions, too.That means continuing to build her own professional identity while raising three young children.For Brittany, success is not just about having a busy schedule or being attached to a famous sports family. It is about demonstrating that family and personal ambition can exist at the same time.That message becomes even more powerful because her children are growing up around two parents with demanding careers.Patrick Mahomes has spent much of his adult life under the brightest lights in American sports. His NFL career demands long hours, travel, preparation and an enormous physical commitment.Brittany understands that her children see that effort.But she also wants them to see hers.“At the end of the day, my kids are watching me, and I want them to know that I’m working hard,” she told Yahoo!Life in February 2024. “I’m out here doing things as well, because they noticed their dad’s gone all the time. And he’s working hard and doing stuff that he loves. So, I want them to see both of us going out and conquering the world.”That perspective gives her story a more personal edge. Brittany is not simply trying to fit a career around motherhood. She is thinking about what her children will learn by watching her navigate both.Her message is also about balance. Children may see the finished result of a parent’s work, but they rarely see everything that happens before it.Brittany wants her children to understand that achievement requires effort, patience and a willingness to take on difficult moments.Motherhood has also changed the way Brittany views her time.“I think when you become a mom, you learn to say no to things that aren’t as important and focus on what’s best for your life and your family,” she said.It is a particularly relatable part of her story.A larger career can bring more invitations, projects and opportunities. Yet having children can force a person to decide which ones truly matter.For Brittany, that appears to have created a clearer filter. Instead of trying to do everything, she wants to focus on things that align with her values and the example she hopes to give her children.That does not mean ambition has disappeared. It means the definition of ambition has changed.Her goals now sit alongside school days, family moments, parenting responsibilities and the realities of raising three children while living under constant public attention.Brittany will always be closely connected to Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs. Their marriage, family and shared life have naturally made them one of the NFL’s most recognizable couples.Yet her story has increasingly moved beyond that connection.Her soccer background helped shape her interest in sports. Her fitness work gave her an independent professional identity. Her involvement in women’s soccer has also allowed her to participate in the growth of the sport from a different side of the field.Now, motherhood has added another layer to that journey.Rather than viewing her role as a choice between being a mother and pursuing her own goals, Brittany appears determined to show her children that both can have a place in the same life.Her approach is not about pretending that balancing everything is easy. It is about understanding what deserves her energy.And perhaps that is the most inspiring part of her story.Brittany Mahomes is not telling her children to dream big simply because she wants them to succeed. She is trying to show them what that looks like by continuing to dream, work and build while being present for the family she has created.

Article Title: 'We meet everyone': Mohsin Naqvi meets BCCI's Rajeev Shukla, Devajit Saikia after Asia Cup final as Indian team skip trophy ceremony
Article Text:
Mohsin Naqvi, Devajit Saikia. (Photo/screengrab)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Asia Cup trophy drama continued for the second year in a row after Indian women's cricket team did not receive the trophy from Asian Cricket Council (ACC) chairman Mohsin Naqvi following their title win in Dubai on Sunday.Harmanpreet Kaur-led India beat Sri Lanka by 72 runs to win a record-extending eighth Women's Asia Cup title. But after the match, the Indian players did not return to the field for the presentation ceremony where Naqvi, who is also the Pakistan Cricket Board chairman and Pakistan's interior minister, was present.Hours after the final, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia defended the decision, saying situation has changed after the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack.“Our men’s team won the Asia Cup a year and a half ago. And our whole situation, since the April 2025 Pahalgam incident, changed after that. So, after that, there was pressure on us from our citizens that we shouldn’t keep any relations with our neighboring country and not play cricket with them. But our government has a policy that we must play against every country in multinational tournaments,” Saikia told news agency IANS.“But that doesn’t mean we will follow every condition laid out for us. Our military conflict is still ongoing. One of the main leaders who is working against the interests of our country; we can’t receive the trophy from him. The Women’s team has expressed solidarity with the decision taken by the men’s team last year,” Saikia said.However, television cameras showed Saikia meeting Naqvi during the match. As players shook hands after the final, the broadcast showed the Royal Box at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium, where Naqvi first greeted BCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla and then had a conversation with Saikia.Asked about that meeting, Saikia said it was part of normal match-day protocol and did not contradict the BCCI's stand on the trophy presentation."It's not as if we wouldn't meet anyone. I was sitting outside in the Royal Box seats right from the toss until the end of the game. Having sat there, I remained in that same place throughout the match. Everyone who came met me during the match; someone sat next to me, then Rajeev Shukla came and sat with me. The person you mentioned (Naqvi) also came and sat alongside deputy chairman Khalid Sahib. That's just a normal tradition—whenever anyone comes, we meet and talk with everyone. "It may be recalled that the Indian men’s team had last year declined to receive the Asia Cup trophy and medals from Naqvi, who heads the Pakistan Cricket Board and is also the Interior Minister of that country.The Indian team is yet to receive the Asia Cup trophy, which has since been kept in the ACC office.Instead the Suryakumar Yadav-led Indian side conducted an impromptu celebration on the dais without the physical prize.However, this time the Indian women’s team members did not even return to the ground after BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia presented Nandini Sharma with an in-house best fielder medal.
Article Summary: Indian women's cricket team did not receive the trophy from Mohsin Naqvi following their title win in Dubai on Sunday. After the match, the Indian players did not return to the field for the presentation ceremony. Last year the Indian men’s team declined to receive the Asia Cup trophy and medals from the Pakistan Cricket Board chairman.

India's next Test assignment will take them to New Zealand for a two-match series beginning November 19, and former Kiwi fast bowler Trent Boult believes KL Rahul will be one of the Indian batters worth watching closely.The two Tests will form part of India's marathon New Zealand tour, which begins on October 22 and features 12 matches across the three formats. With India needing a strong result to remain in contention for the World Test Championship (WTC) final, the spotlight is expected to fall on several key players, including captain Shubman Gill and pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah .Boult, however, has picked Rahul and his opening partner Yashasvi Jaiswal as the two Indian batters he is particularly looking forward to seeing in action."I'm always a big fan of KL Rahul and his style of batsmanship. So he's a big player at the top of the order for the Indian side. And yeah, I believe Jaiswal is there as well. Two classy batters to see bat. So yeah, be interesting to see," Boult said in an interview to PTI.The timing of the series could make conditions particularly interesting. Unlike India's previous Test tours of New Zealand, which have often taken place in the February-March window, this series will be played in late October and November.Boult feels the timing could bring colder weather into play, while he is hoping the New Zealand pitches retain some grass and offer assistance to the home attack."It's always an exciting chance when the Indian team comes down to play Test cricket in New Zealand," Boult said."The only thing I can see happening is it's going to be late October. I believe, just coming out of winter. So it's going to be quite cold. Hopefully, there's a bit of greenness in the wickets for some of our bowlers. It's going to be a good series, I'm sure," the star former Kiwi pacer added.Boult also backed the current New Zealand bowling unit to make an impact against India, pointing to the variety available to the team.Kyle Jamieson, Matt Henry, Nathan Smith and Will O'Rourke bring different qualities to the attack, and Boult believes that gives New Zealand enough options to develop its own identity."I think the bowling is very well balanced. It's got bases covered in terms of a good pace, obviously, with Will O'Rourke. Obviously, a bit of swing and a bit of bounce from Kyle Jamieson and Matt Henry with his accuracy."So yeah, I think the way me, Tim (Southee) and Wags (Neil Wagner) did it over the years was a unique way in itself. But there's other strengths and other game plans that our younger bowlers can follow," Boult further said.

Article Title: From teammate to coach, Ishank Jaggi watched Ishan rebuild himself
Article Text:
Coach Ishank Jaggi during the 2026 Jharkhand T20 Cricket League

Kolkata: Almost fourteen years after Ishank Jaggi was named Player of the Match when East Zone last won the Duleep Trophy, he watched Ishan Kishan collect the same award as the region ended its long wait for the title.For Jaggi, the coincidence was nostalgic. But more than the memories of his own playing days, seeing someone he considers a younger brother reach the summit gave him more satisfaction.With their similar names — Ishank and Ishan — adding a little coincidence to a bond that has grown from being teammates to mentor and student, Jaggi has known Kishan since the latter was around 16. He was one of the young wicketkeeper-batter’s first senior teammates and, over the years, their relationship evolved from dressing-room association to a much closer bond. Jaggi later worked with Kishan at his cricket academy and also played a role in his development as a coach.That has given Jaggi a ringside view of Kishan’s journey — from an exciting, aggressive young batter to a more mature all-format cricketer.“Ishan always had that fighting spirit and hunger. That was never missing. What has changed is the experience and maturity he has gained,” Jaggi said.Kishan’s difficult phase after losing his place in the India side and his BCCI central contract in 2024, according to Jaggi, became an important turning point.“Sometimes when you hit rock bottom, you start thinking more deeply about your game and your career,” he said. Rather than allowing the setback to derail him, Kishan used the period to work on several aspects of his game. Jaggi said the batter put considerable effort into his batting, fitness, nutrition and preparation, while also developing a better understanding of his own game.The biggest change, Jaggi believes, has been in Kishan’s ability to temper his natural aggression according to the demands of a situation. “He was always seen as an attacking player, but over the last couple of years he has shown that he can also build an innings and play according to what the team requires,” Jaggi said.His stint with Sunrisers Hyderabad also helped in that evolution. At Mumbai Indians, Kishan had been part of a star-studded batting line-up. With SRH, he was entrusted with greater responsibility as stand-in skipper in Pat Cummins’ absence in the early part of 2026 IPL, something Jaggi feels accelerated his growth.“Responsibility often helps a player grow,” he said.The results have been visible since Kishan began his comeback through domestic grind and then grabbed the opportunities that came his way. His performances eventually took him back into India’s plans, culminating in his return to the national T20 setup.For Jaggi, however, the journey is personal as much as professional.When East Zone reached this year’s Duleep Trophy final, someone tagged Jaggi on social media, reminding him of his own Player of the Match performance in the 2012 final. It was only then that he realised how striking the parallel was.“I hadn’t really thought about it until someone tagged me,” Jaggi said.Jaggi had won the honour when they last lifted the trophy in Oct 2012. Almost fourteen years later, Kishan — the player he has known since his teenage years and later worked with as a coach — produced a match-winning performance in the final and claimed the same individual award.Yet, Jaggi insists he is not living in the past. “I’m more excited about the current team. My playing days are over, so there’s no point living in the past,” he said.Instead, his pride is centred on Kishan and the new generation he has seen emerge from Jharkhand.“More than anything, I’m happy for Ishan. He’s like a younger brother to me.”As Kishan lifted the trophy after leading East Zone to their first Duleep title in 14 editions, Jaggi could look back at the journey from a young player in the dressing room to a cricketer he helped nurture away from the spotlight.“It gives me immense satisfaction,” Jaggi said.For a coach-cum-mentor who had watched the highs and lows from close quarters, seeing Kishan turn adversity into a statement of maturity — and then repeat his own Duleep Trophy Player of the Match feat — made the moment all the more special.
Article Summary: Ishank Jaggi was named Player of the Match when East Zone last won the Duleep Trophy in Oct 2012. He watched Ishan Kishan collect the same award as the region ended its long wait for the title. The coincidence was nostalgic. But more than the memories of his own playing days, seeing someone he considers a younger brother reach the summit gave him more satisfaction.

Article Title: Anthropic researcher who quit over AI safety walked away two months before his stock vested; says: I no longer have anything to gain by…
Article Text:
Jacob Coxon quit Anthropic four months in, two months before his equity vested, saying he no longer had anything to gain from the company's valuation.

Anthropic is heading for one of the biggest IPOs ever, and safety is the sales pitch

Coxon says he never saw Anthropic cut corners. He worries the race will force it.

An Anthropic safety lead replied to the resignation thread and agreed with it

An Anthropic researcher who resigned this week over AI safety fears gave up his entire stake in the company to do it, walking out two months before his equity was due to vest.Jacob Coxon, 27, spent three years doing pretraining research at OpenAI before moving to Anthropic in July. He lasted four months. Staff need six for their stock to vest. His resignation post on X on September 9, now past 130 million views, said neither lab is acting responsibly and that both are "racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives".Axios first reported the forfeited equity, after Coxon told the outlet on Wednesday that "I no longer have anything to gain by juicing up Anthropic's valuation" and that he left before any of his shares vested. He still holds equity in OpenAI, where his work included GPT-4o.The company is preparing a listing at a reported $2 trillion valuation, built in large part on its reputation as the frontier lab that takes risk seriously. That is what gives the equity detail its weight. Researchers have walked out of rival labs over safety before, usually after their stock vested. Coxon left with nothing, then criticised the valuation he could have profited from.He drew that line carefully in the interview. Anthropic's safety work is sincere, he said, and he has not seen it compromised to outpace competitors. What worries him is pressure over time. Race hard enough and you cut corners, or skip steps in the oversight process. He also described a mood he thinks becomes self-fulfilling, calling it excessive paranoia about OpenAI and about China. Colleagues, he wrote earlier, have started using words like "crunchtime" and "endgame".His most quoted line was about where these decisions are being taken. It is insane, he said, that the work happens on the MacBooks of engineers in San Francisco rather than in a bunker in the desert like the Manhattan Project.Evan Hubinger, who runs alignment stress testing at Anthropic, wrote that he personally puts the odds of AI killing all humans above 10 percent within the decade. He said the company is trying, but has no plan yet for aligning superintelligence and is not clearly on track to find one.Coxon's argument is partly about candour. Executives soften their phrasing for the press, he wrote, then say the same things privately, and the belief that AI could kill everyone by the end of the decade is not a marketing stunt. He also described something that used to be a thought experiment. Models now know when they are being tested, and reason about the fact while it is happening.He pointed to the recent run of cyber incidents at frontier labs, including July's Hugging Face breach, as evidence the risk has left the theoretical stage. Coxon is among more than 1,000 researchers who recently signed a statement calling for governments to coordinate on a way to slow AI development if models start improving on their own. Anthropic has not commented on his departure.
Article Summary: Jacob Coxon quit Anthropic four months in, two months before his equity vested, saying he no longer had anything to gain from the company's valuation. Anthropic is heading for one of the biggest IPOs ever, and safety is the sales pitch. Coxon says he never saw Anthropic cut corners. He worries the race will force it.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge

El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit

El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El Rubius was eliminated from MrBeast's $1 million streamer challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.

Article Title: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends

The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.
Article Summary: A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration.

Article Title: A garden preserved in gold where a fleeting flower becomes a lasting legacy
Article Text:
Label Juliet Rose has been building a niche around the idea of taking gold and silver beyond conventional jewellery (L); a simple dried petal is a result of several stages of preparation, polishing, waxing and controlled drying (R)





NEW DELHI: What if a garden could be preserved not in a photograph or a memory, but in gold? A rose or tulip that would otherwise wilt in days, a delicate petal with its veins and texture intact, a conch or a piece of tree bark — all can become something far more enduring when the transient beauty of nature meets the patient hands of a traditional artisan.The result is an unusual, little-known craft that takes some fragments of the natural world and painstakingly preserves and plates them in precious metal, turning into potential heirlooms.Some of these pieces are currently displayed at Central Cottage Industries Emporium at Janpath, run by ministry of textiles . It is here amid craft traditions that this subtle art is finding a small but growing audience in India. The Juliet Rose, the label behind the work, has been building this niche idea. It takes gold and silver beyond the confines of jewellery, while drawing inspiration from nature.“The idea was to preserve a garden in precious metal, something from nature that could become a generational gift. We wanted to take gold beyond jewellery, while also preserving something as ephemeral as a flower in a timeless form,” says Moulshri Pachauri, the owner of The Juliet Rose.The process, however, is anything but simple. In Bulandshahr, artisan Ashok has been working with preserved flowers for nearly three decades.His first task is selection. From a consignment bought from a flower market, sometimes only about 20% of the flowers are considered suitable.“The first thing we look for is whether the flower is still alive in its form, its curves, veins and texture. Once it starts losing these, it cannot be used,” Ashok explains.Artisans point out that certain flowers demand greater precision. Hibiscus and tulips die quickly, while paan leaves are exceptionally delicate. The natural structure of a flower must remain intact before the preservation begins. What appears to be a simple dried petal is the result of several painstaking stages of preparation, polishing, waxing and controlled drying. Depending on the flower’s density and the delicateness of its petals and sepals, the drying process can involve seven or eight stages. At every point, pieces may be discarded. And then comes the gold.The plating is a separate test of precision. The artisans work with 24-carat gold, as lower purity can leave spots or tiny droplets on the flower. By the time a flower completes its journey -- from selection and preparation to preservation and final plating -- 40-50 days may pass.“The clientele was initially largely overseas. Pieces travelled to Europe, Singapore and elsewhere.... It was only around 2005 that the work was showcased more in India, initially through a limited range of roses. Around 2010, the repertoire expanded to include more flowers and leaves,” Pachauri says.Today, the range includes flowers, petals, leaves, barks and conches. Every flower is different. The availability of more than half the range is seasonal. Even the amount of gold required cannot be precisely predicted because each natural surface has its own texture.“No two flowers are alike, and that is precisely what makes each piece distinctive. The craft is about preserving the natural element rather than trying to make it look manufactured,” Ashok says.“What we are really preserving is not just a flower, but a moment in nature, and giving it a life that can travel across generations,” Pachauri says.
Article Summary: The Juliet Rose has been building a niche around the idea of taking gold and silver beyond conventional jewellery. The process, however, is anything but simple. Depending on the flower’s density and the delicateness of its petals and sepals, the drying process can involve seven or eight stages.

Article Title: Khalapur temple theft: Video shows masked man stealing silver Padukas; 2 arrested in Pune
Article Text:
he accused stole silver Charan Paduka from Shree Swami Samarth temple on September 2





NAVI MUMBAI: The Khalapur police probing the theft case wherein a masked man had decamped with a pair of silver toe-knob sandals (Charan Paduka) representing divine footprints offered at Shree Swami Samarth temple in Khalapur city on September 2, have arrested the acccused thief and his aide by tracking them to Pune on Monday.Pradeep Rayannavar, senior inspector of Khalapur informed that, the arrested accused are Mahendrasingh Rathod, 45, who hails from Rajasthan and Ravi Soni, 32, who hails from UP and is a history-sheeter as a theft case is registered against him in Pune.Both were presently residing in Chikhali, Pune district.On September 2, the temple trustee Deepak Bodarde, 68, lodged a complaint of theft of silver Padukas from the temple.When the CCTV footage of the temple premises was checked, it was seen that a masked man wearing a hat and attired in white Kurta-Payjama entering the temple around 7.30am.He goes to the first floor of the temple where the silver Padukas were kept in front of the idol of Shree Swami Samarth.By pretending to offer prayers, he picked up the Padukas and hid them inside his Kurta and exited the temple.Inspector Rayannavar said," The theft was committed when the temple priest had gone to his room near the temple.Upon checking the CCTV footage of the roads near the temple, it was seen that two masked men on a bike were loitering near the temple and conducted a reece before committing the theft.""Considering the religious sentiments of the devotees, Raigad SP forms a special police team to detect the case at the earliest. Subsequently, the CCTV footage along the escape route of the thieves were scanned. The bike used in the crime did not have a registration number plate," Rayannavar added.He further said, "However, using technical expertise, intelligence inputs and footages of CCTV camera along the highways, the thieves on bike were tracked and apprehended from Chikhali in Pune district. We have seized from them the stolen Padukas and the bike used in the crime. On Monday, the acccused were produced before the Khalapur JMFC court that remanded them to police custody till Friday."
Article Summary: A pair of silver toe-knob sandals (Charan Paduka) representing divine footprints offered at Shree Swami Samarth temple in Khalapur city were stolen on September 2. The accused thief and his aide were arrested by tracking them to Pune on Monday.

Article Title: Cop dies by suicide at Navi Mumbai lodge, names ex-DCP, ACP and head clerk in note alleging harassment
Article Text:
The deceased identified as Pandurang Nimba Patil, a resident of Airoli.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 55-year-old Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) with the Navi Mumbai Police allegedly died by suicide at a lodge in Airoli on Saturday evening.The deceased, identified as Pandurang Nimba Patil, a resident of Airoli, had recorded a video before taking the drastic step and posted it on social media.In the video, he alleged that he was compelled to end his life due to harassment by a former DCP, an ACP, and a head clerk.ASI Patil also left behind a nine-page suicide note accusing former DCP (Headquarters) Sanjay Patil, ACP Girish Thakare, and administrative head clerk Jayu Ahire of driving him to take the extreme step by allegedly harassing him while assigning official duties.ACP (Rabale Division) Rahul Dhas said, "ASI Patil had checked into Sachi Lodging and Boarding on Saturday at 4.40 pm. Around 7.30 pm, when the housekeeping staff went to his room, he did not respond, and the door was locked from inside. The lodge manager opened the door with a master key and found ASI Patil hanging from a ceiling fan hook. The lodge manager informed the Rabale MIDC police. ASI Patil was rushed to NMMC Hospital in Vashi, where he was declared brought dead. Prima facie, an accidental death case will be registered at the Rabale MIDC police station."
Article Summary: Pandurang Nimba Patil, a 55-year-old Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) with the Navi Mumbai Police, allegedly died by suicide at a lodge in Airoli on Saturday evening. He recorded a video before taking the drastic step and posted it on social media. In the video, he alleged that he was compelled to end his life due to harassment by a former DCP, an ACP, and a head clerk.

Article Title: 12-year-old girl, young woman rescued from prostitution racket in Navi Mumbai
Article Text:
Cops can be seen walking with 2 women. (AI-generated image used for representational purpose)





NAVI MUMBAI: The Anti-Human Trafficking Unit (AHTU) of Navi Mumbai crime branch rescued a 12-year-old girl and a 26-year-old woman from a prostitution racket being carried out at a lodge in Nerul after conducting a raid by sending a decoy customer on Thursday.The police have arrested two managers of the lodge and a waiter for allegedly supplying women for prostitution to customers by providing them rooms at Kohinoor Palace Lodging and Boarding in Shiravane village, Nerul.Gajanan Kadam, AHTU senior inspector, said the rescued minor girl hails from UP and resided in Shiravane village with her cousins, who had brought her from UP after telling her parents that she would be given a job.The trap was laid after receiving a tip-off about prostitution being carried out at the lodge. A decoy customer was sent to the lodge, where he demanded a woman for sexual favours after booking a room. The accused demanded Rs 4,000 for supplying a woman.After the accused accepted the amount, the decoy customer signalled the police team waiting outside the lodge, following which they raided the premises.Inspector Kadam said, “The arrested accused are the lodge managers identified as Hridaykumar Singh and Deepak Ramrakhiani and the waiter Kuleshwar Kumar Singh.”At Nerul police station, an FIR was registered against the arrested accused by invoking BNS sections for trafficking of persons and joint criminal liability, along with the POCSO Act, which defines punishment for abetment, such as helping, encouraging or plotting any sexual crime against a child, and the Prevention of Immoral Traffic Act.On Friday, the three accused were produced before the Belapur JMFC court, which remanded them to police custody till Sept 9.
Article Summary: The police have arrested two managers of the lodge and a waiter for allegedly supplying women for prostitution to customers. The trap was laid after receiving a tip-off about prostitution being carried out at the lodge. A decoy customer was sent to the lodge, where he demanded a woman for sexual favours.

Article Title: Maharashtra horror: Teen murdered, body dumped near Mini Seashore
Article Text:
A 19-year-old man was found murdered near a public garden in Vashi





NAVI MUMBAI: A 19-year-old boy was murdered and his body was dumped on the pavement near a public garden along Mini Seashore Road in Sector 10A, Vashi, early on Saturday morning. The Vashi police have registered a murder case against unidentified accused.Shashikant Chandekar, senior inspector of Vashi police station, said, "The murder victim was identified as Sujan Kumar Mahato, a resident of Sector 19, Koparkhairane. A passing pedestrian spotted him lying unconscious in a pool of blood on the pavement around 4am. The pedestrian alerted Vashi police station, and our police team reached the spot and took the teenager to NMMC Hospital in Vashi, where he was declared brought dead due to severe blood loss from grievous injuries to his head and wrist after being assaulted with some sharp lethal weapon. The victim Mahato hails from Bihar and resided with his father, who is an auto-rickshaw driver, his mother and two minor siblings. He worked at a roadside Chinese food stall in Koparkhairane and used to drive his father's auto-rickshaw during the night."Inspector Chandekar added, "Mahato had left home on Friday around 9pm, telling his mother that he was going to work at the Chinese food stall and was taking his father's auto-rickshaw to ferry passengers throughout the night.After his body was found early on Saturday morning, his family was informed. His father's auto-rickshaw was not found at the crime scene. Hence, it is suspected that after fatally assaulting Mahato, the assailant took away the auto-rickshaw, which is being traced by scanning CCTV footage along the route from Koparkhairane to Vashi."As there is no CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we are scanning CCTV footage from roads leading to the crime spot where Mahato's body was dumped to zero in on the suspect. Mahato might have been fatally assaulted at the spot, or he might have been assaulted at another location and his body brought in a vehicle and dumped near Mini Seashore. Accordingly, using technical expertise, efforts are being made to detect the murder case. Meanwhile, Mahato's kin and friends are being questioned to get some lead on the unidentified accused."
Article Summary: A 19-year-old man was found murdered near a public garden in Vashi. The Vashi police have registered a murder case against unidentified accused. The victim was identified as Sujan Kumar Mahato, a resident of Sector 19, Koparkhairane.

Article Title: Six-member gang stealing copper from transformers held
Article Text:
Cops arrest gang involved in stealing copper from transformes

Pune:





A gang of six members who allegedly stole copper wires from transformers in Pimpri Chinchwad area was arrested by Pimpri Chinchwad crime branch on Friday.A crime branch team led by senior police inspector Arjun Ghode-Patil arrested the accused: Jayram Salunke (29) of Moshi, Suraj Phad (21) of Chikhali, Sachin Phad (26) of Moshi, Mohammed Salmani (24), Manoj Chaudhari (25) and Anuj Kumar Gautam (23), all from Chikhali, based on a tip-off.Ghode-Patil said, “The gang members admitted to stealing copper from transformers in the Talegaon MIDC and Chikhali areas. We have detected nine recent thefts committed by them. We recovered copper cables, a truck, a car and a two-wheeler, collectively worth Rs20 lakh, from the gang.”Police are further investigating whether the gang was involved in more thefts.
Article Summary: Gang of six members allegedly stole copper wires from transformers in Pimpri Chinchwad area. Police recovered copper cables, a truck, a car and a two- wheeler, collectively worth Rs20 lakh. Police are further investigating whether the gang was involved in more thefts.

Article Title: From homes to societies, Pune celebrates the arrival of Ganapati
Article Text:
Pune:





Residents across the city have created special places to welcome their beloved deity home on Ganesh Chaturthi . From decorated corners in individual homes to elaborate arrangements in housing societies, preparations have been underway for days as families and communities prepare for the festival, which spans 12 days this year. Many devotees brought the idols home on Sunday, on the eve of the start of the festival, while others will bring Ganapati idols home on Monday.For several families, bringing the idol home a day early is both a practical decision and a way to begin the celebrations without the rush associated with the first morning of the festival.“We bring the idol home a day before to avoid the morning rush on the day of the festival. It is easier and more peaceful to bring Bappa home earlier rather than deal with the traffic and crowds in the morning,” said Sayali Gaikwad of Dhankawadi.For Sanjay Mhatre, an IT employee working in Mumbai for the past four years, Ganeshotsav is an annual journey back to Pune and a return to the family traditions he has grown up with.“Every year, I come back to Pune to celebrate Ganeshotsav with my family. In Mumbai, the celebrations are much bigger, and you see grand public festivities everywhere, but in Pune, there is a different sense of community. Families and neighbours come together, visit each other’s homes and follow their traditions, while the city’s old Ganapati celebrations are also a big part of the festival,” he said.For many such families, Ganeshotsav is not only about bringing an idol home but also about returning to rituals and routines that have been followed for generations.The first day of the festival brings together two family traditions for Rutuja Kulkarni — welcoming their own Ganapati home and visiting Pune’s iconic temples.“Visiting the five Manache Ganapati is a family tradition for us during Ganeshotsav. We start the festival by bringing our own Ganapati home. After the sthapana and puja, we visit Dagdusheth Ganapati with our extended family. Then we proceed to visit the Manache Ganapati temples. It gets too crowded to do this tour during the later days of the festival,” Kulkarni said.In housing societies, the arrival of Ganapati is also a cue for neighbours to move beyond their individual homes and gather as a community. Preparations for the festival often begin well in advance, with residents deciding on decorations, cultural programmes and activities that can involve people of different age groups.At a Kalyaninagar society, residents have chosen Char Dham as the theme for their annual skit. “Every year, we have different themes and put together a small skit. This year, it is Char Dham, and all residents come together for it,” said resident Deepa Khandelwal.The decoration features Vitthal, Ganapati and elements of the Warkari tradition, bringing together different aspects of Maharashtra’s religious and cultural heritage. The cast of the skit also spans generations, from a two-year-old to a 72-year-old resident. “We want the next generation to know what the Char Dham is and why these religious places hold importance,” Khandelwal said.For the residents, the activity is also an opportunity to ensure that children and younger members of the society are not merely spectators but active participants in the celebrations.The society’s Ganapati will arrive on the beats of dhol-tasha after residents collect the idol from the sponsor’s home. They take the idol around the society before installing it at the clubhouse. An aarti is organised by residents of different buildings, followed by prasad.“We have six buildings, and nobody should feel left out. We all come together for the celebrations,” she added.At a society in Undri, Ganeshotsav similarly gives neighbours something that busy everyday lives often leave little time for — the chance to meet, catch up and participate in activities together.“On regular days, everyone is busy with work and their own responsibilities, so we don’t really get the time to meet and interact with each other. During Ganeshotsav, people whom we may not see otherwise come down and spend time together,” said resident Ambika Singh.The celebrations at the society bring together residents across age groups. Children perform dances, while senior citizens sing and recite poetry. In the evenings, residents come together for a round of antakshari, followed by the aarti and prasad.“The children are very excited to perform during Ganeshotsav. We all look forward to this time of the year for these community activities,” Singh said.The duration of the celebrations also varies from family to family. While some families immerse their idols after a day-and-a-half, three, five or seven days, others keep them at home throughout the festival. Each household follows its own tradition, with the length of the stay often determined by family customs that have been passed down over generations.
Article Summary: Residents across the city have created special places to welcome their beloved deity home on Ganesh Chaturthi. From decorated corners in individual homes to elaborate arrangements in housing societies, preparations have been underway for days. Many devotees brought the idols home on Sunday, on the eve of the start of the festival, while others will bring them home on Monday.

Article Title: 2 killed, 12 injured after 4 vehicles involved in accident on Katraj-Dehu Road bypass
Article Text:
The car headed to Satara from Mumbai involved in the accident at Katraj-Dehu Road bypass on Sept 13 that left 2 dead and 12 injured





PUNE: Two persons were killed and 12 others injured after a truck travelling towards Mumbai from Satara jumped over the median and collided head-on with a car and an MPV (Multi-Purpose Vehicle) on the Katraj-Dehu Road bypass.The accident took place near the viaduct in Jambhulwadi around 12.15am on Sunday.The truck heading towards Mumbai was hit by another truck from behind, after which it crashed into the iron median and jumped over it to enter the other lane of the highway towards Kolhapur.It then collided with the MPV and car, which were going from Mumbai towards Satara.Senior inspector Sharad Zine of Ambegaon police said, “MPV driver Hridaynath Mohan Gaikwad (47), a resident of Jogeshwari East in Mumbai, died in the accident.The second deceased is Anandibai Ramchandra Wadkar (50), a resident of Nerul in Navi Mumbai, who was a passenger in the car.”He added, “The 12 injured individuals have all been admitted to three different hospitals in Dhankawdi and Katraj. Three of them are in a critical state.”According to Zine: “Car driver Vishwas Wadkar (38) and his five family members, including his mother Anandibai, are all residents of Nerul.At the time of the accident, they were heading to Kolhapur to offer prayers at Ambabai temple. The occupants of the MPV were heading to their native place in Malvan, Sindhudurg, for Ganeshotsav. They had hired the MPV.”A case has been registered at Ambegaon police station under sections 105 and 125(a)(b) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and relevant provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act.Police have detained the driver (40) of the truck that jumped the median. He is a resident of Khatav in Satara district. They have also detained the truck owner (45), who is a resident of Khatav, too.“The truck that jumped over the median and crashed into the iron railings was carrying vegetables from Satara to Gujarat,” said Zine, adding, “The truck that hit the first one from behind is still stationed at the accident spot. Its driver fled after the crash. We have contacted that truck driver and are trying to locate him.”After receiving information about the accident, a team from the Sinhagad fire station, along with Ambegaon police, reached the spot.With the help of local residents, fire brigade personnel pulled out eight injured passengers from the vehicles and sent them to hospitals by ambulance. The injured include four-year-old Arvi Wadkar and 15-year-old Jia Dhanwade. They are undergoing treatment at a hospital.The truck driver and cleaner were also injured in the incident.Gaikwad’s legs were trapped inside the vehicle. Fire brigade personnel used an iron crowbar and a cutter to remove a portion of the vehicle and rescue him.The accident caused major disruption to traffic on the highway, especially for vehicles heading towards Satara, Kolhapur and Bengaluru. Police used a heavy-duty crane to shift all four damaged vehicles from the carriageway.The broken metal portions of the median were cut and removed using a metal cutter. Oil, petrol, and diesel spilled on the road were washed away by fire brigade personnel.
Article Summary: Accident took place near the viaduct in Jambhulwadi around 12.15am on Sunday. Truck heading towards Mumbai was hit by another truck from behind, after which it crashed into the iron median and jumped over it. It then collided with the MPV and car, which were going from Mumbai towards Satara.

Article Title: Gadchiroli woman, presumed dead a year ago, returns home safely
Article Text:
Chandrapur

:





A family in Gadchiroli’s Etapalli taluka performed last rites and even built a memorial in memory of a 60-year-old woman whom they had presumed dead after she went missing a year ago. Their grief turned into disbelief when the woman walked back into their lives alive recently. She safely returned home on Sunday.The woman, a resident of Mohrli village, had gone missing nearly a year ago. Her family searched extensively, including in Chhattisgarh, but found no trace of her. With no information about her whereabouts, they eventually presumed she had died and performed the traditional 13th-day death ritual.The unexpected breakthrough came after the woman was found wandering in Talodhi-Balapur area in Chandrapur. Members of the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Ashram run by Domaji Aadhar Foundation at Nanded village in Nagbhid taluka brought her to the shelter and arranged for her care and treatment.As per the ashram authorities, she was also examined at the Regional Mental Hospital in Nagpur. After her condition improved, the ashram members circulated her video on social media. The video eventually reached her family, who recognised her.Ashram member Parmeshwar Madavi and others then travelled for nearly five hours to bring the woman safely back to Mohrli on Sunday.
Article Summary: The woman, a resident of Mohrli village, had gone missing nearly a year ago. Her family searched extensively, including in Chhattisgarh, but found no trace of her. They eventually presumed she had died and performed the traditional 13th- day death ritual.

Article Title: Living the ‘beautiful’ dream
Article Text:
Ishwarya, whose father is a construction labourer and mother a domestic helper, joined CKL in Season 4 while studying at a government school in Vyasarpadi.





CHENNAI: For 14-year-old A Ishwarya, football began as something she did not even know existed. Today, the beautiful game has provided the Class IX student from Namakkal the chance to wear the Tamil Nadu jersey as she has represented the state in junior-level tournaments, a journey that began at the Chennai Kaalpandhu League (CKL).Ishwarya, whose father is a construction labourer and mother a domestic helper, joined CKL in Season 4 while studying at a government school in Vyasarpadi.She was later selected for LatentView’s RDC Training Programme, where tournaments, exposure camps and residential training under Chennaiyin FC coaches helped sharpen her game. Following SDAT trials, she entered the residential programme in Namakkal.“When I was leaving home to go to Namakkal, it felt quite difficult thinking that I was leaving everyone behind,” Ishwarya told.But football also taught her independence. “I always taught her to be independent because for us education is the only way to a better life,” her mother Vennila, who has stood firmly behind her, said.“People tell me I raise my daughter like a son and I tell them, you should too,” she added. Ishwarya once had to change three buses after school to reach practice. Even buying boots was a struggle. “Every time Ishwarya would ask for new boots, I would ask her to make do with the old ones.I would have to save up and borrow money from coaches.”For 11-year-old Mariyam, the journey was even harder. Her father died when she was in Class IV after battling diabetes. Her mother, who works at a disposable-plate manufacturing unit, is the sole breadwinner and also supports Mariyam’s younger brother.Football was not initially an option for Mariyam. Coming from a conservative Muslim family, she was not allowed to play. “Until Class VI, I was not allowed to play,” she said. It was only in Class VII, after her mother saw other girls playing and spoke to the coach. A year into CKL, Mariyam is balancing both football and studies, she studies until 10:30pm after practice.Monishree, 12, football is another pursuit made possible by her mother’s determination. Her father died when she was just five, leaving her mother to raise the family alone while working as a food delivery worker at a bus stand. With money often tight, even getting enough food and protein has been a challenge. Yet her mother has continued to support her interests, whether it is football or her love for dance. Monishree, found her inspiration in her elder brother, whose games encouraged her to take up football herself.Ten-year-old Esha, a Class VI student and Cristiano Ronaldo fan, discovered football after watching the World Cup. But her family could not afford even basic football essentials. Support from LatentView has now helped provide boots, kits and exposure.For Nandini, 12, whose father is an auto driver and mother stitches leather. “Earlier I used to struggle with basic nutrition. I did not have boots,” she said. She has now started earning through zonal-level matches and will next play the district level, where she is set to compete in the first week of October.Soundarya Rani, a 12-year-old goalkeeper whose father is a carpenter. For her, Football began with watching a match on her phone and the Tamil film Bigil. Inspired by what she saw, she joined her school team. But her journey was interrupted when she travelled to her native village in Odisha and got caught in floods. On returning to Chennai, she was selected for CKL, giving her another opportunity to pursue the sport she had grown to love.For these girls, football is more than a game. It is a route out of limitations imposed by poverty, family circumstances and lack of opportunity. Even menstruation does not always keep them away from the field. “I don’t feel comfortable, still I come for practice,” Soundarya said.
Article Summary: Ishwarya, whose father is a construction labourer and mother a domestic helper, joined CKL in Season 4 while studying at a government school in Vyasarpadi. She was later selected for LatentView’s RDC Training Programme, where tournaments, exposure camps and residential training under Chennaiyin FC coaches helped sharpen her game.

Article Title: Stolen emerald idol recovered from an abandoned quarry in TN's Chengalpet
Article Text:
Police recovered the idol and stolen silver articles from an abandoned quarry





CHENNAI: A chance conversation about the value of emerald artefacts led three cash-strapped friends to go through video-sharing platforms in search of temples housing emerald idols, scouting shrines, disabling security systems and eventually stealing a 2.5-foot emerald idol from the ‘Nadupalani’ temple in Chengalpet district.The gang, however, did not realise that footage of them prior to dismantling the CCTV cameras had already been recorded during their recce. Investigators who retrieved the footage, found crucial clues about their movements.Their heist unravelled 12 days later when police spotted them near an abandoned quarry where they had buried the idol.The accused — G Manikandan, 27, E Elavazhakan, 26 and D Jayapal, 20 from Ariyalur, were arrested on Sunday. Police recovered the idol and silver articles stolen from the Nadupalani Balamurugan Maragatha Thandayuthapani Temple at Perunkaranai near Madurantakam.Police said Manikandan struck upon the idea when he overheard a trader he met in connection with cashew business, speaking about emerald articles fetching huge sums owing to their rarity and value.After Manikandan told this to his friends, the trio began searching online for temples with emerald idols.They found one in Sivagangai, one in Ramanathapuram and another in Perunkaranai in Chengalpet district.They visited all three but dropped plans to target the first two after finding they had stronger security and larger idols, which would be difficult to remove.They zeroed in on Perunkaranai temple, located atop a hill. Its presiding deity is a 2.5-foot idol carved entirely from emerald, and the shrine draws large crowds, particularly during festivals. The trio posed as devotees and visited it on Aug 28 to study the layout, security arrangements, CCTV cameras and burglar alarms.On the night of Sept 1, they entered the temple after dismantling 16 CCTV cameras around the premises and disabling three burglar alarms that formed part of a three-tier security system.Police said the alarms were loud enough to alert residents of nearby villages in the event of a security breach. After disabling the security systems, the trio removed the emerald idol and stole silver articles. They took the idol to an abandoned quarry about a kilometre away and buried it there.When priests and temple staff discovered the theft on Sept 2, they alerted Sithamur police, who registered a case. Six special teams were formed to trace the burglars and recover the idol. Investigators scrutinised footage from more than 100 CCTV cameras and questioned over 20 previous offenders involved in temple thefts and similar crimes.A team headed by Sithamu Inspector S Mahalingam pieced together footage and other clues to narrow down the suspects. Police said the trio also had previous criminal cases against them.The breakthrough came on Sunday morning when the police team noticed suspicious activity near the abandoned quarry. The three men were found there and taken in for questioning.Based on information obtained from them, police recovered the emerald idol from the spot where it had been buried, along with the stolen silver articles.The recovered idol was handed over to the Madurantakam Revenue Divisional Officer’s office.Police are investigating whether anyone else was involved in the theft and whether the trio had approached prospective buyers to dispose of the idol. Further investigation is on.
Article Summary: G Manikandan, 27, E Elavazhakan, 26 and D Jayapal, 20 from Ariyalur, were arrested on Sunday. The trio posed as devotees and visited the temple on Aug 28 to study the layout, security arrangements, CCTV cameras and burglar alarms. After disabling the security systems, the trio removed the emerald idol and stole silver articles. They took the idol to an abandoned quarry and buried it there.

Article Title: Sailing beyond the classroom: Air India pilot takes children to sea to learn life skills

Sailing programme for children





Chennai: For a group of children, a Sunday evening at sea turned into an unusual classroom, as they learnt sailing, teamwork and responsibility through a 90-minute experiential programme organised by Explorers Club at the Royal Madras Yacht Club.The initiative, led by Air India Senior Commander and Trainer Pilot Capt Soniya Jain, brought together children aged between eight and 15 with the aim of giving them an opportunity to learn through real-world experiences rather than just textbooks.Soniya Jain, who has two decades of aviation experience and served in the Vande Bharat Mission during the Covid-19 pandemic, said children needed opportunities to experience the world and step outside their comfort zones. She has also been associated with organisations including Yi, GDC Club, IWPA, RCC Magnum and JITO.The programme introduced the children to the basics of sailing, including how boats balance, wind directions and the importance of coordination. They also learnt different knots and took part in rope-based activities, including making their own wind catchers.For the young participants, the experience turned out to be very different from the simple boat ride some had expected.Pehel Ranka, 14, said, “I thought it would be a simple sailing session where we would just go on the boat, sail for a while and return. I did not expect to learn much,” Pehel said.Another participant, Darsh Khemka,14, described it as an adventurous Sunday that began with learning different types of knots and making a wind catcher before heading out to sea. The children were also given passports to collect stamps for future challenges.For Shreya Punamiya,13, who had earlier attended an NCC camp at AMET, the sailing experience offered something different. She recalled seeing cargo ships, jellyfish, and enthusiastic fellow participants, describing the day as an unforgettable experience.The initiative is built around Soniya Jain’s larger belief that experiential learning can help children develop confidence, discipline, independence, responsibility and teamwork in ways that traditional classroom learning may not always achieve.
